previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and prostate cancer undergoing radiation therapy was admitted after a pre-syncopal episode at his oncology clinic. He had recurrent Klebsiella UTIs and recent C. difficile infection. On admission, he had sepsis with elevated lactate, leukocytosis, and acute kidney injury. Blood and urine cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, sensitive to cefepime. He was briefly escalated to meropenem due to clinical instability but de-escalated once cultures returned. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotics. Imaging showed hydronephrosis in both native and transplanted kidneys, likely due to prostate obstruction. A Foley catheter was placed for urinary retention. His C. difficile treatment with oral vancomycin was continued. Liver enzymes were elevated, prompting discontinuation of rosuvastatin. He completed two radiation sessions during admission and improved clinically, with normalized labs and resolution of infection markers. He was discharged home with IV cefepime, continued oral vancomycin, and follow-up plans.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
